description: This pie chart, from the paper “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the distribution of four distinct categories: “Right bias,” “Left bias,” “Questionable source,” and an unlabeled fourth segment shown as a gray bar. The chart is divided into four colored slices, each labeled with its category name, percentage, and corresponding count in parentheses. The “Right bias” slice, colored blue, constitutes 30.0% (30) of the total. The “Left bias” slice, colored orange, accounts for 28.0% (28). The “Questionable source” slice, colored green, represents 22.0% (22). The remaining segment, colored gray and labeled with no text, represents 20.0% (20), matching the percentage and count shown for the red “Right bias” slice, which appears to be a mislabeling or error in the chart’s design since the red slice is labeled “Right bias” but the gray slice is the only one without a category name. The chart includes percentage and count labels inside each slice and does not appear to have a separate legend. The slices are arranged in a clockwise descending order by size, starting from the top right.
